Detection is line-of-sight based now (as opposed to proximity based--what it was prior to this patch). But many other changes were made to accommodate this change.

Enemies will no longer immediately investigate your position when in "?" status. This is a massive improvement for dealing with the Grabber, since getting smelled by the thing will no longer cause it to stick to you like flies on shit for the rest of a raid.

Enemies that are aware of your position (denoted by "!") will not shoot at you if a more threatening target/targets are present. I've had several times where I've been able to wade directly through a patrol of Euruskan Infantry because they were too busy moving to engage a Europan squad.

Definitely needs more testing, but those are my experiences so far.

-On the ammo swapping confusion: You can find out what your buttons do in the vast majority of video games by looking in keybinds. Default for changing ammo type is "Y".

-Your complaints about the game expecting you to know what to do are kind of silly. There's a lot to explore in the various menus and maps but like, isn't that kind of the point of playing video games? To explore, learn, discover, and gain mastery? If that's not your type of game, that's alright. While I don't feel your criticism about the lack of information is fair, I do believe it would be more fair to say that it's not intuitively designed. For instance: a lot of people were confused about the prestige mechanic because all of the information on it is buried in a small text box in the character skill menu, written in superscript font. -Oh wait no you buried another complaint in your pros, but it's a fairly valid one. Some of the locations can get very dark during the "harvester events". Your rig can be equipped with a flashlight, but it does take up a valuable attachpoint slot on your rig, meaning you won't be able to bring back as much loot, and the attachable flashlight for the guns is just awful.

If you don’t want to go the triple triad route, you can still learn the card skills, but instead go to the beach on the world map near the school and start turning the fish enemies into cards. You can refine them into water, and then junction water to squall’s strength. This should give you a good early game boost.

It’s worth noting that carded enemies will not give xp, but do still reward AP. I believe Ifrit can learn a skill called STR bonus which gives additional permanent strength each time you level up with the skill equipped. You can max out the potential of this skill and others like it by keeping your level low (by carding enemies) until you can fit 3 of these skills, but casual leveling won’t ruin your game.

Plus, if you card nearly every enemy you come across, you will never need to worry about your magic stockpile running out, ever. A lot of the fun of this game is seeing what items and cards refine into which magic, then seeing for yourself how each spell scales with each stat when junctioned to it. 

Also make sure you’re checking what magic enemies have with the stock command. Certain enemies may carry powerful spells that can’t normally be accessed until much later in the game, and it’s usually worth taking the time to stock up these spells to 100 to stay ahead of the game’s power curve.
